title: Payouts under Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme Subjected to Clawback
what_it_is: Payouts under Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme Subjected to Clawback

sections.label: SIRS scam cases referred to Police
sections.summary: Scams invited non-intended recipients to apply for SIRS payouts, and these cases were surfaced to the Police for investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We are aware that there were scams inviting individuals who were not the intended recipients of the Self-Employed Person Income Relief Scheme or SIRS to apply for payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These cases have been surfaced to the Police for investigation.

sections.label: Erroneous SIRS declarations and refunds
sections.summary: Audit affirmed most applicants' eligibility, but about 0.5% of successful SIRS applications had erroneous declarations, and those applicants were approached to refund payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Subsequent audit affirmed the eligibility of most successful applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But we also uncovered some cases of erroneous declarations, constituting about 0.5% of all successful SIRS applications.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To be fair and consistent to all applicants, those with erroneous declarations have been approached to refund their SIRS payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Some have already done so, and we will reach out to the rest individually to give them time to do so.

sections.label: Number of SIRS refund cases
sections.summary: About 0.5% of roughly 200,000 successful applicants, around 1,000 cases, were approached for refunds, and the number referred to Police was not available offhand.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: What is the number of cases where we have approached the individuals for refunds of the SIRS payouts?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I mentioned in my reply that it was about 0.5% of the successful applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The number of successful applicants is something in the order of 200,000.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There are still some that are pending processing, but 0.5% would come to about 1,000.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To the first question, how many cases have been referred to the Police?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I do not have the number offhand, perhaps if the Member were to file a Parliamentary Question, we could address it appropriately.
